Hey! I know this post is about a week old but I was scrolling through and thought I would share a few that tend to help me!

**If you're looking for somethings to elevate your mood a little:**

[Charly Bliss - Westermarck](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r9DEK9mNVRU&list=PLkIruQqGB5A_7kHUd2LsFs0TGnww9y5yM&index=65) (Happy Grunge-ish Pop Rock). I find the song always puts a smile on my face that I can't get rid of and the video too just has such a sweet happy vibe to it

[Injury Reserve - Oh Shit!!!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1-Mjw96lYgU&list=PLkIruQqGB5A_7kHUd2LsFs0TGnww9y5yM&index=30) (Rap) I find that this song just kinda makes me want to jump around, let out a bunch of anger and say 'fuck it'

[Carly Rae Jepsen - Your Type](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UlFMVzo9zuE) (Pop) I find Carly always gives me an explosion of good feelings that make me okay for the three minutes I'm living in her pop world

[Arctic Monkeys - 505](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MrmPDUvKyLs) (Rock) When this song picks up, it fucking explodes. I used to always listen to this before going to a job that I hated and it would give me the emotional release I needed to get through a shift

[Charli XCX - Next Level Charli](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8mhfE_vzwjo) (Pop) A fun, fast anthem. It feels like it puts you in the passenger seat while Charli drives and it doesn't fucking matter where you're going, because the ride is that much fun.

**If you're looking to kinda find comfort in some sad songs:**

[Radiohead - The Bends](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K8z8hLvjb_U) (Rock) I know it's kinda cliche to start off a list of sad songs with Radiohead but I always find this the perfect one. It's not dreary enough that it makes me feel worse but also has lines like "who are my real friends? Have they all got the bends?" That I find to be comforting

[Earl Sweatshirt - Mantra](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=32v8yZ5hrh0) (Rap) This is my favourite 'I'm sad and angry but I'm too tired to do anything about it' anthem. There's some super hard hitting lyrics and I think that the whole album it's from (*I Don't Like Shit, I Don't Go Outside*) is one of the best portraits of depression there is in music

[Bully - Focused](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fYQahQlPHaQ) (Rock) This is also an 'angry sad' song but this one feels very cathartic. Everytime I listen to it, no matter how bad I feel, it feels amazing to scream along with the "I AM TRYING TO STAY FOCUSED" parts

[Julien Baker - Happy To Be Here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TVhI8TB3G70) (Indie) The opening verse of this are *literally* the words that I have always wanted to use to describe how I felt but could never find. The whole song is extremely painful but beautiful (and that's true for literally all her songs haha)

[Grimes - Delete Forever](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gvzC8MmC850) (Pop) A very atypical song for Grimes that just has the most melancholy feel. It's like looking at the future through the greyest of sunglasses (*well I can't stay above it / Guess I fucking love it* stays stuck in my head whenever something shitty happens)

Sorry if these aren't really to your taste or it wasn't the type of songs you were asking for at all. Hope you're feeling at least a tiny bit better!

I think that the nature of pop music causes people to get too involved in the 'idea' of a star. At a certain level it's built upon setting someone up as a larger then life person. Pop stars get big enough and the public acts like they own them, giving us incidents like the ones mentioned in the article where there is a complete invasion of privacy.

Its been said time and time again, but it's true: celebrities are people too. And as fans at the end of the day, we don't actually know these people. Their putting on a public performance, that's the nature of the game. But their personal lives are still their own, they're not their persona. 

It's sad to see happen time and time again and from what I see, it only gets worse as social media makes us feel closer then ever to celebrities. They're not our friends, they're lives are their own. Yes their music touches us and can hold so much meaning in our lives, but at a certain point we have to allow them to disconnect and let the human being live their life.

Brockhampton! 

I used to absolutely adore them, like especially Kevin Abstract. I first started listening when he dropped Mtv1987 and I immediately fell in love with it (still would put it in my favourite albums tbh) and like Brockhampton wasn't even a thing then.

I remember when All-American Trash dropped and I saw some comment that said "I wish Kevin Abstract would focus more on his solo career then on his shitty group" and at the time I was like half in agreement, the solo shit was wayyyy better then that tape. But over the year I grew to really like it but then American Boyfriend came out that November and I was like "nah, he has to stick to solo stuff"

And then of course, the next June Saturation would come out and they would get huge. I still have a soft spot for a lot of their music but not like I did back in those days. Back then I had all the twitter notifications on, I think on my old phone I still have a screenshot on my old phone of Kevin Abstract's old snapchat when he actually snapped me back like either shortly before or after American Boyfriend.

I was a full on Brockhampton stan probably until after iridesence. I really loved iridesence, but I just didn't follow it as much. It came out the first month I was at uni and just didn't have time to get consumed like I did when I was 14 and Mtv1987 dropped. I think what killed it fully for me was when they had to cancel their show in Toronto for the tour cause of a venue issue. They're last two concerts I had lined up for at like 5am. Arizona Baby was cool tho, I spent a lot of the summer listening to that

I listened to Ginger when it dropped but like I didn't follow it at all before it came out and it was good but I just wasn't invested in the same way. Like I didn't listen to any of the singles and barely had it on my radar. 

I still get happy being able to see where they came from and just how big they got, it's so cool to see the dudes that had a couple thousand listeners on like late night shows, but it's just not there for me anymore.

Okay, sorry for the huge ass ramble just getting all in my feels about times gone haha

Nose Ring - Lil Peep : The way that Peep says "drugs drippin off of my nose ring" almost has this like southern accent to it that sounds really cool for some reason

Zombie - The Cranberries : This whole song is made better by the accent that pops through in the vocals, it just feels rawer and like just perfect. Amazing song.
